title: Case Illustrations — The Catch-Up in a Rebuilt Payment, Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

# Case Illustrations — The Catch-Up in a Rebuilt Payment, Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

The catch-up a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan owes for a cycle not paid is read in one of three ways.

1. Where the plan stands past due at the handling date, the catch-up is the money sent back unpaid in the whole month ending on the handling date spread evenly over the months the term's arrangement runs for.
2. Where the plan stands active at the handling date and a payment on it has been sent back unpaid in that month, the catch-up is the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries spread evenly over those months.
3. In every other case, no catch-up is owed.

The spread figure is rounded to the cent.

## The months the term's arrangement runs for

| Term | 6-Month Deferred Interest | 12-Month Deferred Interest | 18-Month Deferred Interest | 24-Month Equal Payment | 36-Month Equal Payment | 48-Month Bridal Equal Payment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Length of the term's arrangement, whole months | 3 | 3 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 12 |

## Cases (hypothetical)

A plan written on the 18-Month Deferred Interest Plan, whose arrangement runs 6 whole months, carries a scheduled monthly payment of 300.00 USD, and 900.00 USD was sent back unpaid in the whole month ending on the handling date.

| The plan | The catch-up |
|---|---|
| Past due | 900.00 USD spread over 6 months, that is 150.00 USD |
| Active, with that return in the month | 300.00 USD spread over 6 months, that is 50.00 USD |
| Active, with no return in the month | No catch-up is owed |
